introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 3 (0760), Paper 3 - Africa and World History, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing ONE from each of the four sections (Section A: Africa, 1800-1945; Section B: Africa, 1945 to the present; Section C: World Revolutions and Diplomacy, 1700-1919; Section D: World, 1919 to the present date). All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « answer FOUR questions, choosing ONE from each of the four sections ». `regles_choix` porte une règle « 1 sur 3 » par section (A, B, C, D), ce qui correspond exactement à la consigne imprimée ; la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : chaque question porte 25 marks imprimés (« All questions carry equal marks »), soit 100 points pour les quatre questions à traiter. Aucun écart de points constaté ; `points` vaut 25 pour l'exercice et pour l'unique question de chaque fichier.

Sujet scanné de deux pages (page de garde et questions 1 à 12) ; filigranes gcerevision ignorés. Le texte de la page 2 transparaît en miroir sur la page de garde (verso mal opacifié) et quelques espaces sont manquants à l'impression (question 8 : « between1871and1890 », rétabli en « between 1871 and 1890 ») ; aucune question coupée ni illisible, aucune figure ni carte dans le sujet.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level (introduction, développement, conclusion argumentée). Aucune citation n'est inventée et les chiffres sont limités à des repères datés de l'historiographie courante (dates, traités) ; à relire par un historien avant mise en vente.

Question 4 : l'énoncé imprimé date le déclenchement de la révolte Mau Mau de 1951. L'historiographie situe la montée de la violence en 1950-52 (mouvement interdit en août 1950, état d'urgence proclamé le 20 octobre 1952) ; le sujet est recopié tel quel et le corrigé précise la chronologie sans corriger l'énoncé.

Question 5 : l'Afrique équatoriale française regroupe le Gabon, le Moyen-Congo, l'Oubangui-Chari et le Tchad ; le Cameroun, ancien mandat puis tutelle, n'en faisait pas partie. Les interventions militaires françaises (Gabon 1964, Tchad à partir de la fin des années 1960, Centrafrique 1979) et le rôle du réseau Foccart sont cités selon l'historiographie courante, sans chiffres.

Question 7 : le sujet emploie « romanisation » au sens de la promotion du catholicisme romain par Jacques II ; les dates de 1688 sont données en style ancien (naissance du prince le 10 juin, acquittement des sept évêques et invitation à Guillaume le 30 juin, débarquement à Torbay le 5 novembre).

Question 9 : le montant des réparations (132 milliards de marks-or, fixé en 1921) et les pertes territoriales sont cités de mémoire historique établie ; aucune statistique de population n'est avancée.

Question 11 : la Banque mondiale et le FMI sont des institutions spécialisées de l'ONU ; l'UNICEF (fonds et non institution spécialisée) n'est volontairement pas traité. Les dates (variole déclarée éradiquée en 1980, Alma-Ata 1978, convention 182 de l'OIT en 1999, Codex Alimentarius 1963, retrait des États-Unis de l'UNESCO en 1984-85) sont citées selon l'historiographie courante.

Question 12 : le sujet vise la rupture sino-soviétique après la mort de Staline (1953). Les dates (discours de Khrouchtchev en février 1956, rupture de l'accord nucléaire en 1959, retrait des conseillers en 1960, congrès de Bucarest en juin 1960, guerre sino-indienne 1962, incidents de l'Oussouri en mars 1969) sont données selon l'historiographie courante ; aucun chiffre n'est avancé.

Thèmes : les noms sont qualifiés pour éviter les collisions avec les Tags de l'Histoire francophone (`sino-soviet split`, `afrikaner nationalism`, `mau mau revolt in kenya`...) ; plusieurs sont réutilisés des sujets History 2020-2021 (`scramble for africa`, `apartheid in south africa`, `cold war`, `indirect rule in colonial africa`) ; à revérifier à l'ingestion avec `find_tag_variant`.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Carefully examine the manifestations and impact of Bismarck's foreign policy between 1871 and 1890.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** After the unification of Germany under Prussian leadership in 1871, Otto von Bismarck, first Chancellor of the German Empire until his dismissal in March 1890, declared Germany a "satisfied" power that sought peace. His foreign policy had one central aim: to keep France isolated, so that she could not find allies for revenge for the defeat of 1871 and the loss of Alsace-Lorraine, and to prevent a war on two fronts. This essay examines the main manifestations of this policy and its impact.

**1. Manifestations (the main steps).**
- *The Three Emperors' League (1873).* An agreement between the rulers of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Russia aimed to unite the three conservative monarchies against revolution and to keep France without allies. It was weakened by the Balkan rivalry between Austria-Hungary and Russia.
- *The "War-in-Sight" crisis (1875)* showed that other powers, such as Britain and Russia, would not accept a German attack on France, which taught Bismarck to act more carefully.
- *The Eastern Crisis and the Congress of Berlin (1878).* After the Russo-Turkish War, Bismarck presided over the Congress of Berlin as an "honest broker", which reduced the gains of Russia, who felt that Germany had not supported her.
- *The Dual Alliance (1879)* with Austria-Hungary was a defensive alliance directed mainly against Russia and became the core of German diplomacy.
- *The Three Emperors' League renewed (1881)* and the *Triple Alliance (1882)* of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy (Italy was in conflict with France over Tunisia) strengthened the isolation of France.
- *The Reinsurance Treaty with Russia (1887).* After the Bulgarian crisis broke up the Three Emperors' League, Bismarck made a secret treaty in which each side promised neutrality if the other was at war with a third power, except if Germany attacked France or Russia attacked Austria-Hungary. This kept Russia from allying with France.
- *Links with Britain.* Bismarck encouraged the Mediterranean Agreements of 1887 between Britain, Italy and Austria-Hungary, which opposed Russian and French expansion, without committing Germany directly.
- *Colonial policy (1884-85).* After years of reluctance, Germany acquired colonies in Africa (Togoland, Cameroon, South West Africa and East Africa) and held the Berlin West Africa Conference. It was partly used to improve relations with France and to satisfy public opinion at home, and was also a means of creating friction between Britain and France.

**2. Impact.**
- *Peace in Europe.* The system helped to avoid a major war between the great powers for almost two decades, and France remained isolated until the early 1890s. Germany's position in Europe was strong and its economy and industries grew.
- *Limits and contradictions.* The system was so complicated that only Bismarck could manage it. Alliances with Austria-Hungary and Russia could not both be maintained when the interests of these two powers clashed in the Balkans, and the Congress of Berlin alienated Russia from Germany. The German ban on lending to Russia in 1887 also pushed Russia to seek loans in France.
- *Alliance blocs.* Although designed to preserve peace, the practice of secret treaties and alliances accustomed Europe to rival blocs and mutual suspicion, and the annexation of Alsace-Lorraine left France hostile to Germany.
- *After Bismarck.* After his dismissal (March 1890), Kaiser Wilhelm II and Chancellor Caprivi allowed the Reinsurance Treaty to lapse; France and Russia then made an alliance (concluded in 1892-94), which ended France's isolation and created the opposition between the Triple Alliance and the Franco-Russian alliance, a step towards the situation of 1914.
- *Africa.* Colonial involvement led to the German colonies, including Cameroon, with consequences for Africans, though Bismarck regarded colonies as secondary to European diplomacy.

**Conclusion.** Bismarck's foreign policy was a skilful system of alliances and agreements aimed at preserving the new German Empire by isolating France and keeping Russia and Austria-Hungary close to Germany. In the short term it preserved peace and German security, but its dependence on one man and its contradictions meant that it did not survive his fall, and it also helped to form the alliance blocs of the pre-war period.
